fetched.title: Managing Subscriptions and Billing FAQ
fetched.text:
# Where to Manage all of Your Active Subscriptions

#### Subscriptions Tab in User Settings on Desktop

When you’ve purchased a Nitro subscription, or maybe added some Server Boosts to your account, you can manage those subscriptions and find information about them in your **Subscriptions**.

1. Head into your **User Settings** by pressing the **cogwheel** [] **icon**.

2. Then, select the **Subscriptions tab.**

Once there, you can find information about:

* Any active subscriptions;
* The renewal dates and amounts you'll be charged;
* Options to manage your subscriptions, including canceling or switching plans;
* Any gift subscription credits you’ve received.

For more information on how to cancel a subscription, please check out one of these relevant articles depending on your subscription type: Nitro subscription, Server Boosting, Server subscription, or Premium App.

# Billing Information and History

You can find your payment methods on file, as well as your payment history, under **User Settings > Billing.**

#### Billing Tab in User Settings on Desktop

## How do I add or edit payment methods?

You can add a new payment method or edit any pre-existing payment methods in the **Billing tab**.

To add a payment method, select the **Add Payment Method** button and complete the prompts.

#### Example of Adding a Payment Method

If you would like to make changes to a pre-existing payment method, select the **Edit** button to the right of the payment method. From there, you will be able to view the payment method information.

#### Default Tag and Edit Button for Payment Method

You can also set a payment method as **default**. The default payment method will be the first payment method that appears when making new purchases. To select which payment method shows as default:

1. Select **Edit** next to the payment method you’d like to set as the default, or **Add a new payment method.**

2. Select **Make this my default payment method** at the bottom.

3. Press **Save.**

#### Make this my default payment method Checkbox

## How do I change my payment method for my subscription?

You can find the payment method associated with any subscriptions in **User Settings > Subscriptions**. This section will show the payment method you first purchased a subscription with.

If you’d like to change the payment method for your ongoing subscription payments:

1. Open User Settings > Subscriptions.

2. Find the **Pay for it With** section.

3. Select a payment method.

**Note:** Updating your subscription payment method does not automatically change which payment method is set as your default payment method. If you’d like to set one card as both your default and subscription payment methods, you will need to update both settings to the same card. 

#### Pay for it with Dropdown

If you have a Nitro or Boost subscription, the payment method set under the **Pay for it With section** will show a corresponding **Subscription** tag under **User Settings > Billing**.

#### Subscription Tag

## How do I remove a payment method?

1. To remove a payment method, head over to your **User Settings > Billing.**

2. Then, select **Edit** located to the right of the payment method.   
3. While reviewing your payment method details, select **Delete Payment Method** to remove it.

#### Delete Payment Method Button

**Note**: If you have an active subscription, we require you to have at least one saved payment method. If you’d like to cancel your subscription and remove your cards on file, be sure to cancel your subscription first.

## Where can I download my tax invoice or purchase receipt?

1. You can locate either your purchase receipt or tax invoice by heading into your **User Settings > Billing**.

2. Then, select a transaction within your **Transaction History** to review your **Purchase Details**.

3. Within your Purchase Details, depending on which document you have available, you will see  **Download Tax Invoice** or **Download extended purchase receipt > Download PDF**. Once the download is complete, you will be able to review the document.

#### You may see either the **“**Download extended purchase receipt" or "Download tax invoice” within this section.

# What payment methods are accepted?

To make a purchase, you will need a **valid payment method** linked to your account. 

We currently accept the following payment methods:

**Available globally:**

* **Credit or debit card**
* **PayPal**
* **Apple Pay**
* **Google Pay**

**Available by region:**

* **Bancontact** (Belgium)
* **Cash App Pay** (United States)
* **EPS** (Austria)
* **GCash** (Philippines)
* **GoPay** (Indonesia)
* **GrabPay** (Malaysia)
* **iDEAL** (Netherlands)
* **KakaoPay** (South Korea)
* **MoMo Wallet** (Vietnam)
* **Paysafecard** (Germany)
* **Pix** (Brazil)
* **Przelewy24** (Poland)
* **Venmo** (United States)

**Important**: When selecting your payment method, please note we are unable to provide refunds for purchases made with Paysafecards.

# What Discord Purchases Will Look Like on Your Statement

The deed has been done and you completed your purchase, now if you were at all curious how it’ll look like on your bank statements end, it should look like the below!

Here is what you will see if you made a purchase with a **Credit/Debit card** directly:

#### Example of Bank Statement for Nitro Monthly

Here is what you will see if you made a purchase via **PayPal**:

#### Example of PayPal Statement for Nitro Basic Monthly

**Note**: All purchases made within Discord will be labeled **DISCORD\*ItemName** within credit/debit card statements depending on how your bank renders this and **PAYPAL\* DISCORD** if completed through PayPal. If you would like a refund for any purchases, check out our refund policy here.

# Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: My payments are failing, and/or I see pending transactions in my bank statement. What should I do?**

A: Visit our Help Center article to learn more about how to handle failed payments.

**Q: I want to remove all my payment methods, but I can't. What's going on?**

A: Removing payment methods does not end a subscription for you. In order to remove all payment methods, you will need to cancel any remaining active subscriptions first. Visit our Help Center article here for how to cancel your subscriptions.

**Q: What does “proration” mean?**

A: Proration for a subscription means adjusting the cost based on how much of the subscription period you've used. Discord uses this to ensure you’re being charged the correct amount when adding subscriptions or removing subscriptions on your account, and in situations like when accepting a special offer or discount.

**Q: I have a Nitro Monthly subscription, but I just purchased a Nitro Yearly subscription. Can I get a refund?**

A: Your original Nitro Monthly subscription was used as proration credit toward your Nitro Yearly subscription upgrade. This means the amount you paid for Nitro Yearly was not the full amount as you paid the prorated charge. When the subscription renews, you will be charged the full price of the subscription. To check your receipt, check User Settings > Billing.

**Q: What’s the difference between the default payment method and my subscription payment method?**

A: The default payment method determines which payment will show first when making new purchases on Discord. However, your subscription payment method is what’s used to pay for your recurring Nitro and Boost subscriptions.  
You can set the same payment method for both by following the steps to update your default payment method and updating your subscription payment method.

Please note that the payment method used to pay for server and app subscriptions specifically will not show a Subscription tag within the Billing tab, and these subscriptions will charge from either the original payment method selected or the payment method set for the specific App subscription in the Premium App Subscriptions list.

**Q: What happens if I previously purchased a Server Boost subscription, and now I’m buying an additional Nitro Yearly subscription?**

A: If you have purchased any additional subscription with a different billing cycle, **Discord will unify all of your subscription payment dates**. This means that your subscription type may change from a *monthly* cycle to a *yearly* cycle if you have purchased additional subscriptions with a *yearly* cycle.

Additionally, if you purchase an application or server subscription, your Server Boost subscription cycle won't be affected.

For example, if you initially had a Server Boost Monthly subscription, purchasing an additional  Nitro Yearly subscription will convert the current Server Boost Monthly subscription to a Server Boost Yearly subscription in order to simplify all subscription charges to one payment date.

**Q: When making a purchase, I see something called “adjustments.” What is this?**

A: Adjustments can be added to a purchase for a few reasons when signing up for additional subscription purchases, such as:

* If you're changing your billing plan from monthly to yearly
* If your payment is being prorated
* If you are getting a discount

**Q: I’m receiving a “Billing address is invalid” error when making purchase. How do I fix this?**

A: If you see this error while attempting to make a purchase, this means that the billing address associated with the card you are trying to use does not match the address filed with your bank. Please check **User Settings > Billing > Select the card > Edit** and update your billing address.

**Q: Why do I still have server boosts when I canceled my Nitro subscription?**

A: Server Boosts are a separate monthly subscription, and it's possible that you have one or more Server Boost subscriptions active. To manage the subscription, you would need to go to your **User Settings > Subscriptions**.

**Q: I have a new Discord account, can I transfer my Nitro subscription to another account?**  
A: Unfortunately, Discord doesn't currently support transferring Nitro subscriptions between accounts. We understand this might be a bit inconvenient, and we appreciate your understanding.

**Q: I got a notice that my Nitro price is decreasing, why is that?**

A: Discord regularly reviews and updates prices based on factors like your location, local market conditions, currency exchange rates, and regional operating costs. We also test different pricing approaches to better understand what works best for our community.  
As part of this process, we lowered the price of the Nitro plan for a small number of subscribers in the US and Canada on **November 12, 2025**.

fetched.title: Localized Pricing on Discord
fetched.text:
The Euro is available in the following countries on Desktop only at this time: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, and Switzerland.

We’re continually working to make our subscriptions more accessible so you can have more fun on Discord. We offer localized pricing for certain subscriptions and Discord purchases in some countries on the desktop, mobile, and web apps.

What this article covers:

# How do I get local pricing?

* To get localized pricing, you must have a payment method based in a country where Discord offers localized pricing.
* JCB, Discover, Diners Club, UnionPay, and AMEX currently do not support localized pricing. Additionally, certain Brazilian banks do not support BRL.
* If you are using an eligible payment method, you will automatically switch to the new price + currency. The change will take effect at your next billing cycle.
* If you use a payment method that does not support, or are located in a region where Discord doesn't offer localized pricing, our system will automatically charge in USD instead.

# Localized Prices

If localized pricing is available in your region, it may apply to certain purchase, such as:

* Nitro and Nitro Basic subscriptions
* Server Boosts and Server Boosting subscriptions
* Discord Shop purchases

# Frequently Asked Questions

This FAQ is divided into two sections:

## General Localized Pricing Information

Q: What about other countries?

A: We’re always looking to improve Nitro, but we have no updates to share on pricing in other countries at this time.

Q: I’m a desktop subscriber in one of these countries, how come I don’t have localized prices?

A: Go to the Subscriptions page - if you don’t see the localized price listed for your subscription, make sure you have a valid payment method and that the payment method is issued by a bank in one of the eligible countries. You should then receive a popup asking you to confirm your localized price.

Q: How can I see if I am receiving a localized price?

A: The desktop subscriptions settings page will show you what price you are receiving for Nitro. If it doesn’t currently show the localized price, you may still be eligible. Please note that only certain Nitro tiers are eligible for localized pricing at this time, not all.

Q: Why is my price for Nitro different from my friends?

A: Discord regularly reviews and updates prices based on factors like your location, local market conditions, currency exchange rates, and regional operating costs. We also test different pricing approaches to better understand what works best for our community.

If your subscription price changes, we'll always notify you in advance so you know what to expect and can manage your subscription before any new prices take effect.

Q: When does the new price take effect?

A: At your next billing cycle.

Q: Do Nitro Gifts and Shop gifts have localized pricing?

A: Some gifted items, both Shop items and Nitro gifts of all tiers, are available at localized prices.

If paying in your local currency is unavailable, the purchase will default to USD ($). You can see at the final checkout whether your purchase is in localized pricing or USD ($) if you see the relevant currency symbol adjacent to the price. A purchase in USD looks like: “$X.XX”.

Q: I still can’t pay for my Discord purchases or subscriptions because [X] (e.g. you don’t accept my payment method).

A: We’re trying to improve support for purchasing Discord subscriptions, including Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Server Boosting, as well as purchases from the Discord shop in various countries.

Q: Why were there additional fees or taxes on my purchase in a localized pricing country?

A: When making a purchase in a country where localized pricing is available, mandatory fees and/or taxes may be imposed. Please reach out to your bank or payment processor if you have questions about taxes or fees.

Q: I purchased a Nitro/Nitro Classic Monthly or Yearly subscription before localized pricing became available in my country. Can I get a refund?

A: We are happy to issue a refund for your purchase if it falls within our Refund Policy. If your purchase falls within the refund policy, you can reach out to our support team here to request a refund: dis.gd/billing

If your purchase falls outside the refund policy, our team is unable to issue a refund. However, your subscription will automatically be updated to the new localized price upon the next renewal date. We appreciate your understanding!

Q: How do I know if a price is in my local currency?

A: Each currency displays with its specific currency code (for example, €, ฿, ¥) or in format CA$X.XX. If you’re in a region with localized pricing, any USD-denominated pricing will be presented with $, USD, or US$. beside the price.

## Specific Location-Based Information

Q: Why was I charged in USD for my purchase despite being in a region where localized pricing is available?

A: To clarify, you may have been charged in USD for a purchase (including Nitro, Server Boosts, or Shop items) despite localized pricing being available in your region for any of the following reasons:

* Your payment method on file does not originate from the proper region where localized pricing is available.
* Your payment method does not support the currency you’re attempting to pay with (for example, PayPal.)
* You’re using a VPN, which may affect proper recognition of your location.
* You’re purchasing through a third party vendor, such as Google Play, that does not support transactions in all currencies.
* You purchased a gift. Gifts are not currently available in all localized prices, and will cost the equivalent of the USD price, or default to USD, depending on your region.
* You manually selected USD as your currency in the “Pay for it with” menu during the checkout process.

Q: My bank in Brazil won't process my payment in BRL. What should I do?

A: We are aware of this issue and working on a fix with our payment providers. We apologize for any inconvenience! In the meantime, you can try switching to an alternative payment method, which may resolve the issue.

Q: Why did the PLN pricing in Poland change after December 14, 2022?

A: To clarify, on December 14, 2022, we grandfathered our previous Polish prices as we expanded Euro pricing availability to our Polish users.

If you subscribed to Nitro, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting before this date, you will keep your current pricing as long as you don't make any further subscription changes. Such changes include but are not limited to: changing billing frequency, changing plan tier, changing payment methods, adding or removing boosts, requesting a refund, or any other changes to your subscription features, price, or billing period.

If you’d like to cancel your subscription, you can do so by going to User Settings > Subscriptions. However, keep in mind that canceling your subscription will also result in a loss of grandfathered prices once your subscription ends.

Q: Is localized pricing available for ARS/Argentina?

A: As of February 15, 2024, we began the deprecation of ARS pricing and it is no longer available when purchasing Nitro, Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, and/or Server Boosting. If you are a Discord user in Argentina and currently have a Nitro, Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, and/or Server Boosting subscription, you will receive a notification of this change through the email associated with your Discord account about how this change will impact your subscription.

If you would like to cancel your Discord subscription, you can go to your User Settings > Subscription to cancel your current subscription(s).

Q: I lost my grandfathered pricing on my subscription, how can I get it back?

A: Unfortunately, once grandfathered pricing is lost, Discord Support cannot restore it to your subscription. This typically happens when you make changes to your subscription.

Changes that affect grandfathered pricing include: changing your billing frequency, switching plan tiers, updating payment methods, modifying boosts, requesting refunds, or making any adjustments to your subscription's features, price, or billing period.

Q: Did the TRY/Turkey pricing change for Discord subscriptions?

A: On February 21, 2024, we made a price adjustment to the TRY pricing for our Discord subscriptions, which is in effect for all new purchases of Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic in Turkey. For current subscribers of Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic in Turkey, you should see a notification of this change through the email associated with your Discord account about its impact on your subscription.

If you would like to cancel your Discord subscription, you can go to your User Settings > Subscriptions to cancel your current subscription(s).

If you are currently subscribed to Nitro, Nitro Basic, and Nitro Classic through the Apple App Store or the Google Play Store and you are based in Turkey with the TRY pricing, you will maintain the legacy subscription prices so long as you are still subscribed through the mobile app.

Q: I’m in Great Britain or Canada and I see my price is now localized. When did this happen?

A: As of April 2026, we transitioned pricing in Great Britain and Canada to local currencies. This change standardizes pricing across these regions and provides a more consistent and simplified purchasing experience.

fetched.title: Overview of Discord Apps - Documentation - Discord
fetched.text:
A **Discord application** is the core entity that represents your integration with the Discord platform. Every bot, Activity, and Social SDK integration is backed by an application registered in the Discord Developer Portal.
Applications hold your credentials, OAuth2 settings, bot configuration, and metadata. Whether you’re building a simple command-response bot or a full game integration with voice chat and rich presence, it all starts with creating an application.


## The Three Types of Discord Apps

### Bots

Bots are automated user accounts operated by application code. They appear in servers with an `APP` tag and can respond to events, slash commands, and user actions.
Use bots when you want to:

* Add commands, moderation tools, or utilities to a server
* React to events (messages, joins, reactions) in real time
* Build interactive experiences with buttons, menus, and modals
* Post automated updates from external systems

Bots can be **guild-installed** (added to a specific server) or **user-installed** (available everywhere the user goes, without requiring server permissions).

### Activities

Activities are embedded web applications that run inside Discord channels. They’re built with the Embedded App SDK and can be launched by any user in a channel or from a bot with the `LAUNCH_ACTIVITY` interaction callback.
Use Activities when you want to:

* Build a game or interactive experience that runs inside Discord
* Create collaborative tools (watch parties, drawing apps, trivia games)
* Leverage Discord’s existing social context: voice, friends, servers

### Social Layer for Games

The Discord Social SDK lets you add Discord-powered social features to your game across PC, mobile, and console. You can integrate individual features alongside your existing social systems or build out a more complete Discord-powered experience.
Use the Social SDK when you want to:

* Add rich presence, friends lists, and voice chat to your game
* Support cross-platform social features with Discord account linking
* Let players interact through Discord without leaving your game

## Where Apps Install

| App Type | Install Target | What It Unlocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bot (guild-installed) | A server | Access to server channels, members, events |
| Bot (user-installed) | A user | Available in DMs, group DMs, and any server |
| Activity | An application | Launchable from any voice channel |
| Social SDK | Your game | Social features embedded in your game client |

## What APIs Can Apps Use?

There are a handful of different APIs that you can pick and choose from based on your app’s functionality and which Discord features you want to access. Below is a quick overview of the main APIs on the Discord developer platform, but you can read more details and information about API usage in the API reference.

### HTTP API

The **HTTP API** is a REST API that lets you interact and modify core Discord resources like channels, servers (or guilds), users, and messages.
Use the HTTP API to:

* Retrieve information about a resource
* Create, update, or delete a resource

Read details about using the HTTP API in the API reference.

### Gateway API

The **Gateway API** is a WebSocket connection between your app and Discord. While it’s most commonly used to receive a real-time stream of events from Discord, the connection is bidirectional. Your app can also send events to Discord over the same connection.
Use the Gateway API to:

* Receive real-time events from Discord (messages, member joins, reactions, voice state changes, and more)
* Update your bot’s presence and status
* Manage voice state and connect to voice channels
* Perform the connection handshake and manage the lifecycle of your Gateway connection

Read details about using the Gateway API in the API reference.

## Start Building

## Bots & Companion Apps

Build a bot that responds to events, commands, and user interactions in Discord servers.

## Social Layer for Games

Add Discord-powered social features to your game using the Discord Social SDK.

## Activities

Build an embedded web app or game that runs inside Discord voice channels.
